## What it does
1. Stall net: a fifth check in pa_presence (`fyi-stall` presence claim). A seat with 2+ peer FYIs, idle, the oldest 15 min old, gets one notice per backlog sent to its PA, or to the prime if there is no live PA. The notice lists each FYI's sender, age and fenced first line and gives `pij-rs fyi-read --seat <s> --pending` (new, read-only). The seat is never woken. The claim records newest_ms, so a newer FYI re-arms it.
2. Sender guard: `pij_core::fyi::hold_warning` adds an actionable warning to the receipt. It never refuses.
3. and 5. Wording: horse's review a-h, plus row 9. Receipt: "held (fyi), <seat> was NOT woken". Cold-wake refusal row: "only if they need do nothing; wakes no one". The golden fixture and MANIFEST.toml were re-recorded.
4. PA line: a "Waiting FYIs: …" line on turns handed to a pa-role seat. It is computed at hand-over and never stored: in `claim_inbox_inner`, in the pane worker (`DrainWorker::with_notes`, with a per-job cache so retries type the same text), and at admission only for the direct socket and typed rungs. Capped at 300 bytes; the stall notice is budgeted to 2048 bytes delivered.
6. F170: `fyi_notes::refreshed` and `pij_core::fyi_watch::refresh_notice` mark held large-seats: and idle-nudge-fyi: notices when they flush and when they are read. Sizes come from `Services.seat_sizes`, which the presence round writes.
- Kestrel owns delivery/** and was told twice, by FYI, about the delivery/mod.rs edits.
